subject: Critical response banding and pricing concessions for ACME pilot
messages:
From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-sys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Enterprise SLA ask for ACME pilot

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our leadership is comfortable moving the pilot to a production-like environment in Q1, but procurement flagged SLA and escalation coverage as prerequisites. A few concrete asks from our side:

- Uptime bands (99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) and the corresponding per-month credits. How do you cap credits over a quarter?
- Response windows for P1/P2/P3 and on-call escalation coverage (names or roles acceptable) — we need guaranteed escalation to an engineering on-call within X minutes for P1s.
- Can you reserve a small pool of guaranteed on-call hours each month (retainer) and what is the pricing?
- Pricing concession: if we commit to a 36-month reserved capacity and a staged rollout across two regions, can we get a multi-year discount, and what's the interaction with SLA credits?

I attached our RFP excerpt. Can you send a written proposal we can share with procurement (Anya Sokolov cc'ed)?

Jordan
Director, Cloud Ops — Acme Systems

Attachment: ACME_RFP_2026.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-sys.com>
Cc: Anya Sokolov <anya.sokolov@acme-sys.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 12:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enterprise SLA ask for ACME pilot

Jordan / Anya —

Appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise proposal we can take to procurement; happy to follow with a one-page summary for your legal team. High level: we can support multi-year discounts tied to committed throughput + a retainer for guaranteed escalation coverage. Details: 

- Uptime bands & crediting (monthly):
  • 99.9% (Standard): 5% of monthly invoice credit for that month
  • 99.95% (Enhanced): 10% credit capped at 1.5x monthly invoice spread across quarter
  • 99.99% (Premium): 25% credit capped at 3x monthly invoice across quarter
  - Quarter cap defined to limit retroactive credit exposure for large volume swings.

- Response windows (SLA):
  • P1 (system down / data-loss risk): initial ack < 15m, engineering on-call engaged < 60m
  • P2 (major feature/latency): ack < 30m, engineering triage within 4h
  • P3 (minor/quality): ack < 8h, product-level response next business day

- Escalation & retainer:
  • We can reserve 40 hours/month of SRE retainer for ACME as part of a premium bundle (reserved retainer billed monthly). Retainer hours cover fast-tracked escalations, prioritized bugfix/patch windows, and quarterly runbooks.
  • Additional on-call blocks available at hourly rates or converted to credits when unused.

- Multi-year pricing concessions:
  • 12-month commit: 15% effective discount on hosted list rates
  • 24-month commit: 18%
  • 36-month commit: 22% (conditional on minimum throughput commit and two-region deploy)
  • One-time onboarding credit available for 36-month deals (applied to first invoice)

- Interaction with SLA credits: credits apply to invoice in the month of occurrence subject to the quarterly caps above; discounts are applied to list pricing before credit calculations. We can add a small exception for catastrophic events defined in contract.

Next steps:
1) If the pricing bands above look directionally right, I’ll draft a short commercial term sheet + SLA appendix.
2) Please send expected monthly token & peak QPS estimates — this will let me firm up the committed throughput bands and precise pricing.

Attached: Redwood_SLA_Tiers_20261220.pdf, Redwood_Pricing_Calculator_20261220.xlsx

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0191

From: Jordan Pike <jordan.pike@acme-sys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Sokolov <anya.sokolov@acme-sys.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Enterprise SLA ask for ACME pilot

Karthik —

Thanks, that’s a helpful starting point. A few follow-ups from procurement & ops:

- Escalation specifics: procurement wants a named escalation path (e.g., Tier 1 support → SRE on-call → Engineering lead). Is Redwood willing to identify the team roles and provide a primary contact (role-based is fine) for P1s?
- Retainer size: 40 hours/month is reasonable. Can you provide a flat monthly retainer fee and the on-call hourly overage rate?
- Discount ask: ACME’s CFO is pushing for 20% on a 36-month commit with a clause for true-up at year-end. Is 22% your absolute ceiling or negotiable in exchange for a slightly higher committed monthly baseline?

Procurement (Anya) will take the commercial term sheet; can you include the proposed DocuSign-ready clause language for quarterly credit caps and the true-up mechanics?

On the usage side: initial pilot estimate — 45M tokens/month, peak 120 QPS, expected growth 30% YoY.

Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Enterprise SLA ask for ACME pilot — need pricing approval & concession sign-off

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding the thread with ACME. They asked for: 36-month commit + two-region deploy; retainer (40h/mo); and a potential 20%+ discount. They estimate 45M tokens/mo, peak 120 QPS.

Requesting quick guidance: are we comfortable offering 22% for 36 months (conditional on the throughput floor), or should we cap at 18% and offer a one-time onboarding credit instead? Also need a pre-approved flat monthly retainer rate to put in the term sheet and a clear SLA credit cap we can include in DocuSign language (procurement asked explicitly).

My recommended commercial: 36-month / 22% / onboarding credit $50k / retainer $25k/mo for 40h (includes 24/7 escalation triage) — but I want finance/legal input before I put in writing.

Can you reply with the concessions you’ll sign off on? If approved, I’ll draft the term sheet and loop Legal.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Enterprise SLA ask for ACME pilot — need pricing approval & concession sign-off

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick read: we can meet ACME in the middle. Approvals below (subject to Legal sign-off on true-up and credit cap language):

- Discount: offer 18% on a 36-month committed deal by default. We can stretch to 20% only if they raise committed baseline by ~15% (so the economics work for the cluster sizing).
- Onboarding credit: approve $35k applied to the first invoice (not refundable).
- Retainer: flat $22k/month for 40 hours (covers triage + 8 emergency hours / month). Overage billed at $650/hr or converted to credits at invoice discretion.
- SLA credit caps: keep quarterly cap at 3x monthly invoice for the 99.99 band and 1.5x for 99.95; add explicit carve-out for force majeure (Legal to craft wording).

Ask Legal to prepare the DocuSign-ready term sheet with: quarterly cap language, true-up mechanics (annual reconciliation on usage with pre-agreed escalation to increase commit), and a clause documenting retainer hours + conversion mechanics. Marissa, can you own the term sheet drafting?

If Legal signs off, I’m comfortable with the above being the committed offer to ACME.

Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Ops — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
